ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Anti-Money Laundering (revised 2024, effective January 1, 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3, effective November 1, 2024); Provisions on the Administration of Foreign-Invested Enterprises (State Council Order No. 743); Company Law of the PRC (revised 2023, effective July 1, 2024); Measures for the Administration of Foreign Investment Information Reporting (SAMR Decree No. 41) and the Administrative Measures for the Record-Filing of Foreign-Invested Enterprises.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation or equivalent registration certificate of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the foreign parent's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the parent jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention member state: notarization by a local notary public followed by issuance of an Apostille certificate by the designated competent authority; no Chinese consular legalization required. If the parent jurisdiction is not a member state: notarization by a local notary public, certification by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the parent country, then legalization by the Chinese Embassy or Consulate having consular jurisdiction over that jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar or equivalent authority of the foreign parent's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path where the issuing jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention State: notarize the registrar certificate, then obtain an Apostille from the competent authority. Non-member state path: notarize, authenticate through the issuing country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. The authenticated document must be accompanied by a Chinese translation prepared by a certified translation agency where required by the local SAMR office.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation of the WFOE and designating the legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors or equivalent governing body of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague member states: notarize the signatures and board authority, then apply for an Apostille via the designated competent authority. For non-member states: notarize, authenticate via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the issuing state, then submit to the Chinese Embassy or Consulate for consular legalization. Deliver the notarized and authenticated original, with a Chinese translation, to the local SAMR-approved agent for filing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum and Articles) of the foreign parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent entity or its registered agent in the parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Where the issuing jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille Convention state: notarize the articles, apostillize at the competent authority, no Chinese consular step. For nonmember jurisdictions: notarize, authenticate through the parent country's foreign affairs ministry, then obtain consular legalization from the PRC embassy or consulate with territorial competence over the parent jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter confirming the foreign parent's banking relationship and source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution of the foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague member state bank: banker's signature notarized, then Apostille from the competent authority. Non-member state bank: banker's signature notarized, then authenticated by the issuing state's designated authority and finally legalized by the Chinese consulate. The WFOE's future RMB bank account opening and the capital contribution remittance will require this letter to be reviewed by the receiving Chinese bank together with the authenticated copy.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign Investment Information Report initialization form signed by the would-be legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent or its authorized incorporation agent; filed through the SAMR Integrated Online Platform with automatic sharing to the Ministry of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic filing instrument; no notarization or apostille required. It is submitted electronically through the yzt.samr.gov.cn portal and signed via legal representative personnel digital authentication. If a foreign signatory cannot complete the digital signature, a notarized and apostilled or consular-legalized signature page may be required by the local SAMR office, following the same parallel Hague Apostille versus consular legalization rule based on the signatory's residence jurisdiction.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, directors, legal representatives, supervisors, general managers, and authorized signatories must undergo mandatory screening against the PBOC politically exposed persons database, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN sanctions lists, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the Chinese Ministry of Public Security suspicious and criminal intelligence databases. For a low-risk executive search and headhunting WFOE, enhanced due diligence requires verification of source of wealth and source of funds for any shareholder or UBO found to be a PEP or a senior political figure, with written compliance sign-off. Periodic screening must be repeated at every incorporation milestone, at capital injection, and before each dividend or retainer wire distribution, with a full documented audit trail retained for no less than five years under PBOC Order No. 3.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System via the SAMR Integrated Enterprise Registration and Name Pre-approval platform (State Administration for Market Regulation online at yzt.samr.gov.cn or the provincial counterpart portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE's statutory Chinese name must consist of administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry or operating characteristics + company form (有限公司). The trade name shall be written in standard Chinese characters (Simplified Chinese) and may incorporate a phonetic or semantic transliteration of the foreign parent's brand if the parent provides a notarized authorization and the transliteration does not mislead the public. Pinyin romanization is not a substitute for Chinese characters in the registered name, although a corresponding English name may be recorded for banking and taxation ancillary use. The total name length is subject to municipal SAMR administrative rules, generally between 2 and 12 Chinese characters for the distinctive segment. The name must not imply state organ, charitable, financial, or licensed placement functions that the WFOE does not yet hold, nor use the term 人力资源 or 猎头 unless the corresponding HR service license is included in the pre-incorporation approvals.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receiving a formal rejection from the SAMR name pre-approval online platform, the applicant must first confirm the written administrative rejection reason within 3 working days and determine whether the rejection is due to a formatting defect or a substantive conflict. If the rejection is based on similarity with an existing registered entity or prohibited token, the applicant may revise the administrative division and distinctive segment and resubmit through the same platform immediately; a resubmission does not require a fresh notarized parent authorization if the parent's name authorization is already filed. If the applicant insists on the same name, the legal representative or an authorized Chinese attorney must file an administrative reconsideration with the municipal Administration for Market Regulation within 15 calendar days of the rejection decision under Article 41 of the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC, accompanied by the original parent brand authorization, trademark registration certificate or coexistence consent letter from the prior registrant, a comparative table of the two names, and a statement of legitimate business interest. If administrative reconsideration fails, an administrative lawsuit may be filed with the competent People's Court within 15 calendar days of the reconsideration decision. During the appeal, the reserved name window expires unless extended by the SAMR; therefore, it is advisable to apply for a fresh reservation with a fallback name immediately. The entire appeal process should be budgeted at 20-45 days and must be closed before any lease signing, licensing, or bank account application is executed, since the WFOE's legal personality is not yet in existence. In large municipalities such as Shanghai and Beijing, most rejected names can be resolved by a formal consultation with the Enterprise Name Pre-approval Section of the local SAMR before filing a new application; appeal statistics show that about 70 percent of administrative reconsiderations relating to trade names are decided in favor of the applicant when the name is not absolutely prohibited and the similarity dispute is defensible. However, for the token 猎头 or 人力资源, the applicant must first obtain the Administrative License for Human Resources Service from the local district or municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau before SAMR will approve the name. The license must therefore be obtained simultaneously with or before the name clearance application, and the license number must be attached to the incorporation dossier.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding address is generally rejected for a WFOE in the executive search and headhunting industry. The Company Law of the PRC and the Regulations on the Administration of Company Registration require the registered address to be a physical premises actually used by the enterprise for its principal business or administrative management. The local SAMR office will cross-check the property ownership certificate or lease agreement, and the tax authority will conduct a verification of the business premises before issuing the tax registration certificate. For a headhunting agency, the local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau will, during the license review, require that the applicant has an independent office with dedicated workstations, a meeting room for confidential interviews, secure file storage, and evidence of normal business operation. Consequently, commercial mailbox addresses and co-working virtual addresses are admissible only if the co-working operator accepts a formal sub-lease for an actual assignable desk, the lease term is at least 12 months, and the operator provides a written business premises usage confirmation letter acceptable to SAMR, the HRSSB, the tax agency, and the commercial bank. A pure postal mailbox without a physical reception desk, meeting room, and staff presence will not satisfy the requirement and will be treated as false registration, subject to a fine of up to RMB 50,000 and deregistration. For the target payment rails, the receiving bank will also conduct a physical visit and require the company name sign at the door before opening the RMB basic bank account and drafting foreign exchange settlement instructions for retainer wires.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical inspection: (1) company name plate at the entrance matching the registered name; (2) the legal representative or a designated manager physically present; (3) employment contracts and social insurance registration records of local employees; (4) original Human Resources Service License displayed at the office; (5) financial bookkeeping and invoices physically or digitally stored on-site; (6) client retainer agreements and search assignment files with confidentiality safeguards; (7) interview rooms and phone lines; (8) adequate business equipment including computers, telecommunication hardware, and office furniture; (9) lease agreement and property owner identity or property ownership certificate; (10) tax registration certificate posted or available electronically. The quantified risk of unannounced inspection by municipal tax or SAMR authorities for a newly incorporated WFOE in the headhunting industry is moderate: approximately 25-35 percent within the first 12 months of incorporation, and materially higher if the company appears on any abnormal-operation alarm list because of a change in registered address, a mismatch between the declared business scope and actual invoicing, or an employee social insurance contribution record showing zero insured staff. Random checking rates in Shanghai, Beijing, and Guangzhou are around 5 percent annually, but targeted inspections occur whenever the HR license annual reporting, foreign investment information report, or cross-border capital inflow triggers a SAMR or tax warning flag.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: State Council and National Development and Reform Commission tariff policy: registration fees abolished; a nominal RMB 50-100 data service or certificate printing fee may apply in certain municipal windows.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and competent authority (e.g., HK Companies Registry authenticated copy and Apostille Office or Singapore Notaries Public / Singapore Academy of Law), plus courier to China

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary public, apostille competent authority, or Chinese Embassy consular legalization section, and Chinese translation agency
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 150-300 for notary plus Apostille/legalization, translated at RMB 250-400 per page by a SAMR-accepted certified translation firm.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized and authenticated copy of Articles of Association of foreign parent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary, apostille authority or Chinese Consulate, and Chinese certified translation agency
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market tariff for notarized copy plus Apostille or consular legalization, translation and courier, where the originals are kept with the home registry.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank Reference Letter from foreign parent's bank
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign parent's banking institution and notary/public authority of the bank's jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank corporate service fee (USD 50-150) plus notarization and Apostille/consular legalization fee as applicable.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO and sanctions screening report by a licensed compliance data provider (PBOC Order No. 3 filing and OFAC/UN/PEP screening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed third-party AML compliance data vendor and incorporated compliance counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for one-time entity-level enhanced due diligence screening, official UBO report generation, and audit trail storage for five years.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 6, 10, 23-25, 28, 47-50 and 68-75; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020), Articles 6, 17, 31-33; Regulations on the Administration of Company Registration of the People's Republic of China, Articles 2, 8 and 14-16.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Municipal Administration for Market Regulation of the city where the registered office is located, under the State Administration for Market Regulation, together with the Ministry of Commerce foreign investment information reporting node.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application Form and the duly executed bilingual Articles of Association, submitted through the National Enterprise Registration online portal and the local Market Supervision Administration one-stop acceptance window.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital for a general WFOE under national company law; the subscribed capital stated in the Articles is the legal capital charge, and shareholders must pay all subscribed capital in full within five years from incorporation under Article 47 of the 2023 PRC Company Law. If the local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau imposes a minimum paid-in capital requirement for talent-intermediary license applicants, commonly RMB 100,000 to RMB 200,000, that amount must be paid in and evidenced before the Human Resources Service License is issued. No blocked escrow account is required by national law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] CO., LTD. ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT ON [DATE]. RESOLVED: 1. Incorporation and Articles of Association. The creation of the Company as a limited liability wholly foreign-owned enterprise and the filing of its bilingual Articles of Association are hereby ratified and approved. The Board confirms that the business scope shall be limited to executive search, headhunting, talent mapping, C-Suite search and specialist technology recruitment services as set forth in the Articles, and no licensed activity shall be commenced without the required Human Resources Service License. 2. Share Capital Subscription. The sole shareholder subscribes for the entire registered capital of [Currency and Amount], consisting of [Number] ordinary shares with a par value of [Amount] per share. The capital schedule attached as Exhibit A is adopted. The legal representative and the finance officer are directed to collect all capital contributions and to deposit them in the capital contribution bank account before the statutory payment deadline prescribed by Article 47 of the PRC Company Law 2023, and to obtain proof of payment for all licensing filings. 3. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office located at [Full Address] is adopted as the statutory office and service address of the Company for all official notices, tax correspondence, and legal process. Management is directed to register the office lease and to obtain the fire safety inspection certificate before operations begin. 4. Banking Authorization. The Company shall open corporate bank accounts with [Bank Name]. The General Manager and the Legal Representative, together with the Chief Financial Officer, are authorized to execute account opening forms, bank mandates, and e-banking authorization, subject to dual-signature approval for transactions above [RMB threshold]. Retainer receipts may be collected via wire transfer and WISE B2B payment accounts, and such accounts shall be disclosed in the banking AML and KYC review. 5. Statutory Officer Appointments. [Name] is appointed as Legal Representative, [Name] as General Manager, [Name] as Supervisor, and [Name] as Compliance and Data Protection Officer. Each officer shall hold office and may be removed in accordance with the Articles of Association. 6. License and Compliance Directive. Management is directed to apply for the Human Resources Service License before earning any revenue from headhunting, to complete tax, social insurance, housing fund, and foreign investment information reporting, and to maintain corporate seals under a recorded custody policy. 7. Financial Year and Auditors. The first financial year starts on the incorporation date and ends on 31 December; an independent auditor shall be appointed. The Chairman is authorized to certify a true copy. DATED on [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Business Scope Structuring
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Administration for Market Regulation via the National Enterprise Name Registration System; consultation with the district Human Resources and Social Security Bureau for HR-license compatibility.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare three proposed company names such as [City][Brand] Human Capital Consulting Co., Ltd. and submit them through the National Enterprise Name Registration System. In the application, define the business scope in language compatible with ISIC 7830, using approved governmental wording covering talent recommendation, senior executive search, headhunting, interview and career planning services. Verify that the stated registered capital is sufficient for the intended human resources service license threshold and that the proposed office address is suitable. Retain the enterprise name confirmation code and the system-generated application reference because the code will be needed for the Market Supervision Administration filing in Step 3.
required_dossiers: Completed enterprise name pre-approval form with three alternative names
Office site intent letter or lease with property owner consent
Copy of foreign investor certificate of incorporation or national identity document
Proposed bilingual Articles of Association and business-scope text
Foreign investor board resolution authorizing the WFOE establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to identical or confusingly similar existing enterprise names, replace it with the second or third alternative name and resubmit; if the business scope is queried, delete unlicensed wording, add a restrictive clause supporting headhunting only, and obtain a written confirmation from the Human Resources and Social Security Bureau before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legalization, Apostille and Chinese Translation of Foreign Investor Domicile Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public and Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the foreign investor's jurisdiction; Chinese Embassy or Consulate; or the Chinese-designated apostille authority where the Apostille Convention applies.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: At least 90 days before the Market Supervision Administration filing, obtain a certified copy of the foreign investor's certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and board resolution authorizing the Chinese WFOE. If the investor's jurisdiction is a party to the Convention on Apostille, attach the apostille certificate; otherwise, legalize each original through the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Each document must then be translated into Chinese by a certified translation company and submitted with an affidavit from the translator affirming completeness. The translation must be aligned with the Articles of Association and the foreign investor's registered legal name.
required_dossiers: Foreign investor certificate of incorporation
Certificate of good standing or equivalent issued within 90 days
Foreign board resolution authorizing WFOE establishment
Apostille or consular legalization certificate
Certified Chinese translation and translator affidavit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authentication chain is rejected, obtain a supplementary apostille or consular certification from the competent authority in the foreign jurisdiction and re-deliver the package; inaccuracies in the translation may be cured by submitting a corrected certified translation within the registry's correction window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Establishment Registration and Foreign Investment Information Reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Administration for Market Regulation one-stop service window via the National Enterprise Registration Information System, followed by the physical window where required by the municipality.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Company Establishment Registration Application Form using the confirmed enterprise name, legal representative details, registered capital, and registered office address. Attach the bilingual Articles of Association, first board resolution, legalized foreign investor documents, office lease and property ownership certificate, passport copies, and appointment letters for officers. The legal representative must sign the electronic application and authorize the company seal after issuance. The registry will issue the Business License and Unified Social Credit Code. Immediately after registration, the system forwards the establishment information to the Ministry of Commerce foreign investment information reporting system, and the company files any supplementary information within 20 working days.
required_dossiers: Company Establishment Registration Application Form
Bilingual Articles of Association
First board resolution and shareholder written consent
Office premises lease and property ownership certificate
Apostilled or consular-legalized foreign investor documents with certified translations
Passport copies and appointment letters for directors, supervisor and general manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Market Supervision Administration issues a correction list or administrative interview, respond within the prescribed correction period by amending the business scope, registered capital, residence certificate, or office address; if the application is rejected, correct the defects in the electronic record and reopen a new submission without losing the name approval if it remains valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Seal, Tax, Bank, Social Insurance, and Human Resources License Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau seal filing window; Tax Service Bureau of the State Taxation Administration; local branch of a licensed commercial bank; Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one business day of obtaining the Business License, have the company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal and contract seal engraved by a Public Security Bureau-authorized seal engraving enterprise and complete the seal filing. Within 30 days, complete tax registration at the local Tax Service Bureau, set up invoice quota and electronic fiscal filing, and register social insurance and housing fund for the first employees. Open a RMB basic account and a foreign-currency settlement account at the company bankers. Before offering paid retainer services, apply at the Human Resources and Social Security Bureau for the Human Resources Service License; the license approval process includes an office inspection and a personnel qualification review. Ensure a written data protection and AML policy is adopted before the first retainer wire or WISE B2B transaction is accepted.
required_dossiers: Business License and Unified Social Credit Code
Public Security Bureau seal engraving filing certificate
Articles of Association and first board resolution
Paid-in capital contribution vouchers or bank certificate
Office lease, property certificate and fire safety inspection certificate
HR license application form, staff resumes, employment contracts and professional qualification certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social insurance registration is delayed, consult the Tax Service window and submit the missing Unified Social Credit Code and lease; if the HR license application is denied, appeal through administrative reconsideration to the provincial Human Resources and Social Security Department within 60 days or rectify the staffing, paid-in capital, or office deficiencies and reapply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau Talent Market Administrative Office; fire-safety and workplace clearances are coordinated with the district Fire and Rescue Section and the district Emergency Management Office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Human Resources Service License (Talent Intermediary Permit) issued under the Regulations on Human Resources Market of the State Council; an Internet Content Provider filing must also be completed if the headhunting service operates a recruitment portal or database website.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment and the local Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau; no EIA filing path applies to office-only ISIC 7830 activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable - pure office-based executive search and headhunting, not listed in the 2021 EIA Classification Catalogue; no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operation; no Environmental Impact Assessment report or registration form is required for ordinary leased office premises.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable at production scale; no process wastewater, volatile organic compounds, or hazardous waste will be generated. If the office is fitted with a kitchenette or restroom, domestic sewage must be discharged through the municipal network and meet local sewer standards (COD not exceeding 500 mg/L and BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L unless a stricter local limit applies), and all indoor finishing materials shall comply with national indoor air quality limits for formaldehyde (0.10 mg/m3) and total volatile organic compounds (0.60 mg/m3) after fit-out.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must be covered by the building fire safety acceptance certificate or fire inspection certificate issued by the district Fire and Rescue Section, together with fire extinguishers, two emergency exits, emergency lighting, and a fire drill plan. If candidates and clients regularly visit the office, a Fire Safety Certificate for public-use premises is required before the first candidate interview. The workplace must pass the structural load verification contained in the lease or property certificate and the workplace hygiene inspection by the municipal health authority, and the employer must complete worker injury insurance and social insurance registration before deployment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; electronic filing through the official e-Tax portal (Electronic Tax Bureau) operated nationally and via provincial STA websites
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Incorporate the WFOE at the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and obtain a business license containing the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC). 2. Within 30 days of incorporation, the WFOE legal representative must log into the local STA e-Tax platform to complete the post-incorporation taxpayer registration ('tax registration information confirmation'), where the USCC becomes the legal Taxpayer Identification Number for all direct taxes and VAT. 3. Submit the external legal representative identity proof, Articles of Association, registered office lease, bank account information, and financial/accounting officer appointments. 4. Select VAT registration status: either 'small-scale taxpayer' (for annual service sales below RMB 5 million) or 'general VAT taxpayer' (for larger operations or voluntary election to claim input VAT credits). 5. Register for electronic invoice issuance on the STA's digital electronic invoice platform; this platform authorises the generation of fully digitalized e-invoices with a compliant tax control code. 6. For the foreign non-resident parent/shareholder, no separate Chinese TIN is required for the WFOE; if the parent receives dividends, the parent must supply a Chinese foreign tax residence certificate to claim any applicable tax treaty relief from dividend withholding tax. 7. All statutory registrations are bank-linked and visible to the STA's Golden Tax phase IV system for real-time compliance monitoring.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: VAT taxpayer-elective classification: a small-scale taxpayer may elect to register as a general VAT taxpayer and thereafter cannot revert. Corporate Income Tax (CIT) does not permit look-through or check-the-box elections; the WFOE is a China resident enterprise taxed on worldwide income at 25%. No hybrid-mismatch or US-style check-the-box elections exist under Chinese tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration threshold for business entities; every enterprise must register for VAT upon obtaining its business license. Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration applies when annual taxable service revenue exceeds RMB 5,000,000, with voluntary election available for smaller service entities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China employs a real-time fiscal invoice clearance mechanism under the Golden Tax System (GTS phase IV). VAT invoices, including both ordinary VAT invoices and Special VAT Invoices (SVIs), must be issued via the STA-approved electronic invoice service platform. Fully digitalized electronic invoices (FD-EI) are generated with a unique tax control code, transmitted to the STA instantaneously, and supported by mandatory API-based integration for high-volume issuers. There is no separate physical stamping requirement; the tax control code serves as the anti-fraud fiscal stamp. All invoice data is subject to continuous automated cross-matching between VAT output invoices, input credits, corporate income tax, and bank transaction data within the STA's tax digitisation infrastructure.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods exports, the 0% VAT zero-rating applies automatically upon compliance with customs export procedures and foreign exchange repatriation rules. For executive search/headhunting services (classified as consultancy/modern services), Chinese VAT law under Ministry of Finance Circular Cai Shui [2016] No.36 generally provides VAT exemption rather than zero-rating for services rendered to overseas clients and wholly consumed outside mainland China. To qualify, the WFOE must prove: (i) the services are supplied to a non-resident client, (ii) the services are performed and consumed entirely outside China, (iii) the price is negotiated on a commercial arm's-length basis, and (iv) the foreign currency consideration is received and repatriated into China through a licensed bank. For services that fall within national zero-rating categories (e.g., R&D, design, international freight onward), the same documentary and repatriation requirements apply to claim a 0% output VAT rate.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Cross-border service contract (bilingual or English) specifying the headhunting deliverables and overseas consumer; commercial invoice issued by the WFOE; evidence of overseas consumption, including client engagement emails, meeting records, and final placement reports showing executive search output used entirely abroad.

Bank Foreign Exchange Income Declaration (FX income report issued by the Chinese receiving bank under SAFE reporting rules) evidencing the receipt of overseas payments and the currency conversion/remittance into the WFOE's domestic account.

For any incidental goods exports (e.g., recruitment marketing materials): Customs Export Goods Declaration (Chinese Customs Export Declaration Form), Bill of Lading or Airway Bill, and Export Collection Verification receipt from the remitting bank.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unverified or fraudulent zero-rating/exemption claims attract comprehensive STA audit scrutiny. If the STA determines that the exported services were not wholly consumed abroad, or that the customs/FX documents are forged or non-authentic, it will retrospectively reverse the VAT exemption/zero-rating, claw back the unpaid VAT for up to 5 years (with no time limit in cases of fraud), charge daily late-payment interest of 0.05% of the unpaid amount, and impose administrative fines of 50% to 500% of the under-declared tax under the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection. Criminal exposure under Article 204 of the Criminal Law (fraudulent export tax rebates) applies where the WFOE uses false documentation or fictitious export transactions; penalties can include incarceration of responsible individuals and confiscation of assets. Additionally, SAFE and the State Administration for Market Regulation may impose separate foreign-exchange control penalties for unlawful cross-border receipt or retention of funds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) acting jointly with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Chinese renminbi (RMB) is fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade in services such as executive search and headhunting retainer fees, subject to genuine transaction documentation and standard bank verification. Capital account transactions, however, operate under a registered and supervised system: a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) must register its foreign investment with SAFE or a delegated bank under the Foreign Investment Information Reporting regime, and only then may the foreign shareholder inject capital. Injected foreign currency is converted to RMB at a domestic bank under a single capital account settlement rule, and the RMB funds are credited to the WFOE's capital account or a renminbi capital escrow account. For profit repatriation, the WFOE must complete annual audit of financial statements, file corporate income tax returns, and verify that the distributable profits are derived from real operations; remittance abroad is processed by the bank against audited profit distribution resolutions and the Foreign Exchange Business Registration Certificate. There is no general surrender requirement for export proceeds since the 2012 reform, but all foreign exchange receipts from current account activities must be repatriated and either retained in a current account or settled with a designated bank; a formal reconciliation against the State Administration of Foreign Exchange monitoring system is mandatory. In practice, structural pain points include the need for registered capital to be fully injected within the business term, strict use of the capital account prohibition on providing equity financing to third parties, and the difficulty of converting RMB retained earnings into hard currency without a complete statutory audit trail. For a headhunting WFOE with intangible service invoices, the bank will demand robust contracts, staff payroll evidence, and tax payment receipts for every remittance, as service trade is treated as high-impact for money laundering due to the absence of physical goods. Overall, RMB is convertible for operating income and remittances of after-tax profits, but every cross-border flow must be mapped to an approved purpose code and cannot be netted or arbitrarily offset.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The People's Republic of China does not mandate a fixed statutory conversion ratio for export proceeds. Under the current SAFE framework, a WFOE may retain foreign currency receipts in an export settlement current account or independently decide to settle them into RMB. However, all export proceeds must be repatriated to China within the timeframe specified by the terms of the trade contract, generally no later than the payment due date, and must be received through a designated foreign exchange bank. The bank will require exhibition of customs declarations, invoices, and trade service contracts; if the receivable remains outstanding beyond the statutory reconciliation period (normally 90 days for general trade, extendable with justification), the WFOE must file a trade foreign exchange receivable deferral registration with SAFE. For executive search services, there is no physical customs declaration; the trigger documentary dossier includes the signed headhunting agreement, timesheets, candidate placement reports, and cross-border invoice; banks will treat such service export proceeds as current account income and allow retention or settlement at the WFOE's discretion, subject to anti-money laundering screening. The core legal obligation is timely repatriation, not conversion, and a failure to repatriate warrants penalties under the Measures for the Administration of Foreign Exchange in Trade.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Renminbi/foreign currency registered capital received) , Basic Operational Current Account in RMB, and Service Trade FX Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Account (registered capital injection) and Current Account for Service Trade Receipts and Disbursements
Capital Escrow Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account for Operational Expenses
Basic Foreign Exchange Account and RMB Current Account for Payroll and Retainer Disbursements

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Practically non-viable for a China domestic WFOE treasury. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, or Airwallex are not licensed to maintain local RMB capital accounts or deliver services against SAFE regulations. While Wise B2B can be used to submit certain outward remittance instructions in theory, the funds must first be domiciled in a duly licensed Chinese bank current account; the EMI itself cannot act as a receiving bank for foreign direct investment capital injections, cannot issue foreign exchange receipts for capital account verification, and cannot interpret Chinese statutory reporting obligations to the PBOC/SAFE. Furthermore, China's Rules for the Administration of RMB Settlement of Cross-Border Trade require that cross-border settlement be handled by a domestic designated bank with a direct CNAPS/SWIFT interface. An offshore EMI would merely be a payment instruction aggregator and would still require a corresponding domestic bank sponsor, which defeats the compliance purpose. The only allowable niche is for employee expense reimbursement or outbound service payments after the underlying RMB has already been settled in a domestic bank, but even then, the corporate bank's approval is required. Hence the underwriting recommendation is to rely exclusively on Tier-1 Chinese banks and treat the EMI as an auxiliary reporting tool only, never as the primary liquidity rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly established WFOE with foreign investment structure, the statutory legal representative (if a foreign national) and the general manager must generally appear physically before the bank's compliance officer to open the capital account and to complete the Foreign Exchange Business Registration. In key metropolitan branches, a remote video interview may be accepted for non-capital current accounts, but the capital account opening and the first capital injection verification require either physical presence of the legal representative and at least one director or a notarized Power of Attorney (PoA) authenticated by the Chinese embassy or consulate in the director's home country, plus a certified passport copy and a board resolution authorizing the appointee to sign the account documents. In practice, nearly all Tier-1 banks will insist on one physical branch visit for the legal representative or the authorized deputy for the initial onboarding, especially when the shareholder is an intermediate holding company in Hong Kong or Singapore. Post-onboarding, account signatories can operate via corporate internet banking with Hardware Security Tokens (UBank tokens) and two-factor SMS authentication; no further physical appearances are necessary unless the beneficial ownership structure changes. The branch will also require the original Foreign Enterprise Legal Person Business License, the Articles of Association, the Foreign Investment Information Report certificate from the Ministry of Commerce (or a filing code), the tax registration certificate, the seal registration record, and the SAFE Foreign Investment Registration Code. Hence the practical mandate is a one-time hybrid process: remote preparation of documents, then one in-branch compliance interview for the legal representative or the designated liaisonholder with an authenticated PoA.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) appears solely as a nominee or a shell holding entity in a low-tax jurisdiction; the bank's screening flags a mismatch between the statutory shareholder and the actual controller of the WFOE, particularly where the parent entity is registered in the British Virgin Islands or Cayman Islands and exercises a high degree of opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full chain of ownership leading to the natural person ultimate controller, including certificates of incorporation, register of directors and shareholders, trust deeds or foundation resolutions, up-to-date beneficial ownership registers, and a written declaration of the source of wealth and source of funds for each shareholder. Notarized and apostilled (or Chinese consulate-legalized) copies of the UBO's passport pages, three years of audited parent company financials, a bank reference letter from the parent's home bank, and a detailed corporate org chart showing why the WFOE is a legitimate executive search business rather than a pass-through.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The WFOE's stated principal business is executive search and headhunting, which is an intangible service with high revenue concentration in invoice-based billing. The bank fears that cross-border retainer payments may be used to disguise commissions, kickbacks, or the repatriation of funds from illicit sources, especially when the WFOE bills large sums to a single overseas client without demonstrable payroll or recruitment deliverables.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a complete employment and service delivery trail: signed executive search engagement letters with a clear fee clause, candidate placement agreements, candidate interview schedules and evaluation reports, placement confirmation letters signed by the client, linked payroll records for placed candidates (when the WFOE is also the employer of record), time sheets for retained search projects, and a monthly forensic reconciliation between invoices and actual candidate placements. Also submit the WFOE's business licenses with the specific people resources service permit or talent intermediary license, plus a notarized management letter from the statutory auditor confirming that service revenue is supported by substantive contracts and that no third-party payment settlement is used to obscure the pathway.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from an offshore parent is structured as a series of small, frequent wire transfers (Splitting or 'smurfing') instead of a single registered capital injection, triggering structuring red flags under Chinese AML Circular 11 and the PBOC's Administrative Measures for Financial Institutions' Anti-Money Laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the board resolution authorizing the full registered capital subscription and a capital contribution schedule showing the intended multi-tranche injection timeline with corporate wealth evidence for each tranche, including overseas bank statements, dividend declarations from the parent, or proceeds from a private equity round. The treasury team should execute the entire capital injection in a lump sum whenever possible; if tranches are mandatory, the WFOE must file a modification of foreign investment registration with SAFE before the first tranche and attach a binding written capital payment plan to the bank's compliance team, plus a legal opinion from a Chinese counsel confirming the structure is a standard WFOE equity investment, not cash-flow laundering.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The WFOE intends to fund operations through a mixing of service trade revenue (retainer fees paid in foreign currency), local RMB operating income from Chinese clients, and proceeds of intercompany loans, creating a commingling of current and capital account flows that the bank cannot reconcile automatically.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a funds-flow matrix that includes the specific SAFE purpose codes for every transaction category, a segregation undertaking confirming that capital account funds will be held solely in the dedicated capital deposit account, and a treasury policy manual ratified by the board requiring all operational income be booked to a separate RMB current account. The WFOE must also appoint a compliance officer to submit quarterly reports to the bank showing sources of funds, reconciling all cross-border receipts with invoices and contracts, and stating that no capital account funds were used for working capital beyond permissible categories. The bank will require a sworn affidavit, a legal opinion on the separation of capital and current accounts, and an internal audit report of the first 12 months of treasury operations.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital for the WFOE must be routed as a direct SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's bank to the WFOE's designated capital account at the chosen Tier-1 Chinese bank. The remittance instruction must include the payment purpose code '621011 – foreigners' capital contribution to establish a foreign-invested enterprise' under the SAFE categorization, and the remitter must be the legal shareholder as recorded in the Foreign Investment Information Report. The receiving bank will wait for the transaction to hit its Foreign Exchange Monitoring System and then request the capital verification report from the statutory Chinese certified public accountant before approving the settlement of foreign currency into RMB. Once the RMB is settled, the funds must be placed into a capital deposit account with a restricted use: they can be used only for the WFOE's own operations such as payroll, rent, purchase of office equipment, and business expenses; they cannot be lent to affiliates or used to acquire real estate for non-operational purposes. For additional working capital, the WFOE may raise an intercompany loan subject to the 'macro-prudential adjustment coefficient' ratio set by the PBOC, whereby the borrowing limit is based on the enterprise's net assets; the intercompany loan must be registered with SAFE, and the inbound creditor's account must be identified via a full name and a purpose code '622 – foreign loans from non-residents'. Both capital injection and intercompany loans require a follow-up SAFE Foreign Exchange Business Registration update within 15 days of the change, and each disbursement to third parties must be supported by an invoice, a contract, and a tax withholding voucher where applicable. The critical interlock is that the bank's anti-money laundering monitoring will tag the WFOE's capital account if settlement exceeds the declared investment amount or if the source of funds does not match the registered beneficial owner; hence the treasury department must maintain a centralized register of all inbound MT103 messages and reconcile them to the SAFE system daily.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the executive search and headhunting business, outbound trade disbursements principally consist of retainer fee remittances to overseas subcontractors, referral partners, or international payroll agents, and dividend payments to the offshore parent. The preferred clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for all single payment obligations under USD 500,000, using the appropriate SAFE purpose code: 'Services – Management Consulting and Talent Services' (322 for current account service fee payments) or 'Profit Distribution' (320) for dividends. The bank will require a complete documentary estate for each MT103: a synthetic invoice with the exact description of the executive search service, the underlying client contract, the candidate placement evidence, and a tax deduction declaration for the contractor if the payment is to a non-resident entity. For higher-value placements where the WFOE is the prime contractor and must ensure quality and delivery, a documentary collection (D/P or D/A) is permissible for the export of services? In practice, international service trade does not use shipping documents, so a banker's acceptance or a commercial letter of credit is rare; however, a standby letter of credit (SBLC) from the client's bank can be provided as a payment guarantee for large retained search mandates. The most operationally efficient route for recurring monthly retainer payments of five to ten accounts is to enforce a payment factory arrangement with the domestic bank: the WFOE uploads a bulk payments file in the bank's proprietary format, the bank screens the beneficiaries against OFAC, EU, and UN sanctions lists, and then releases the RTGS/CHIPS or SWIFT transactions in one batch. For outbound dividends, the bank must verify the audited financials, the tax completion certificate for withholding tax (WHT) paid on the dividend, the board resolution declaring the dividend, and the SAFE profit repatriation form; the funds are then settled directly without further review. The clearing rail is always MT103 through the domestic bank; no third-party netting or e-wallet settlement is permitted for a WFOE's regulated trade and dividend flows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB/USD foreign exchange spot transactions are available for current account service trade receipts and payments; the bank requires genuine transaction documents and does not permit speculative trading.

Enterprises can enter into plain-vanilla forward contracts with the commercial bank for the purpose of hedging the WFOE's receivables or payables, with the underlying trade contract evidenced and the contract maturity aligned to the expected cash flow; banks usually require a 10-20% margin guarantee, but a corporate credit line can substitute.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are strictly prohibited for onshore China entities; the deliverable USD/RMB forward contract is the only permissible instrument, and settlement must be on a deliverable basis at maturity through the domestic bank; any offshore NDF on the RMB must be managed by the offshore parent, but the WFOE itself cannot participate.

Cross-currency swaps are permissible only where the WFOE has long-term foreign-currency-denominated liabilities (e.g., an external intercompany loan), and the swap must be for debt servicing, interest, and principal repayment, with SAFE registration of the loan underlying the swap and prior written approval of the domestic bank.

Financial derivative products that embed a leverage feature, optionality beyond a plain-vanilla European forward, or any payout pegged to an asset price are not permitted without a specific demonstration of the corporate treasury need and prior FX derivative investor qualification assessment by the bank.

For operational hedging of a continuous invoice flow, rolling forwards with monthly or quarterly tenors can be executed under a master FX agreement with the bank, provided the total notional does not exceed the projected service trade income validated by the WFOE's board-approved annual budget and historical revenue trajectories.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Information Publicity Report (Annual Return / Annual Report Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS), with integrated sharing to Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 1 and June 30 for the immediately preceding calendar year; no extensions available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failing to file by June 30 places the company on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operating Status within 10 working days; if unresolved for 3 consecutive years, the company is placed on the Serious Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise List, leading to administrative blacklisting, revocation or forced cancellation of the business license, and disqualification of directors and senior officers from forming or managing companies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Enterprise Annual Information Report (FDI Annual Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) through the joint SAMR/MOFCOM/SAFE integrated annual reporting platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before June 30 for the prior calendar year; the WFOE must confirm equity, beneficial controller, actual business scope and FDI data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit or submission of false data triggers an administrative rectification order; may result in a penalty under the PRC Foreign Investment Law, cancellation of foreign-exchange capital-flow facilitation, denial of subsequent capital project/SAFE registration, and recording on the enterprise credit violation platform

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement and Reconciliation Return (Enterprise Income Tax Annual Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) through the competent local tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to May 31 of the year following each calendar tax year; quarterly prepayments are reconciled in the annual settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underpaid tax attracts a daily surcharge of 0.05% until payment; civil penalties range from 50% to 5 times the underpaid tax; failure to file can attract a penalty up to CNY 10,000 per return and credit downgrade, but does not automatically strike off the entity unless enforced by tax authority and accompanied by long-term non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Financial Statements Audit Report (WFOE Mandatory CPA Audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent certified Chinese accounting firm licensed by the PRC Ministry of Finance; the signed audit report is required for the SAMR integrated annual report and is available for tax authority inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audit work must be completed in time to support the annual SAMR/MOFCOM report; for a calendar-year WFOE this is effectively by May 31 of the following year to accompany the CIT final settlement and annual information report; internal completion target is 4 months from the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to have an audited financial statement makes the annual report incomplete, exposes the company to abnormal-operations listing, triggers tax audit red flags, and can result in administrative penalties under the PRC Accounting Law and Foreign Investment Law; severe or repeated violations may lead to revocation of the WFOE license

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Human Resources Service License Operation Compliance Return (Executive Search/Headhunting Business)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau (HRSSB) responsible for the Human Resources Service License
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 in most provinces and cities, or within 90 days of the licensing anniversary if the local rules use the anniversary model; must cover active headhunting operations, basic service data, fee structures and staffing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit the annual operation report or conduct of business without the valid license is treated as unlicensed operation; the HRSSB may issue a fine, order removal of all executive-search advertisements, suspend or revoke the Human Resources Service License, and coordinate with SAMR to cancel restricted business scope or the entire WFOE license

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Individual Income Tax Consolidated Return and Employee Withholding Tax Annual Reconciliation (Foreign/Resident Staff Compliance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) via local tax authority under the jurisdiction of the WFOE; applicable to salaried executive-search employees and seconded foreign consultants
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Resident employees must complete annual individual income tax reconciliation between March 1 and June 30 of the following year; the employer's annual withholding report is due within the same statutory tax-calendar window, with monthly/quarterly withholding obligations throughout the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate reconciliation creates personal tax arrears, daily interest surcharges at 0.05%, administrative penalty up to 3 times underpaid tax for serious misreporting, and public credit/visa consequences for non-resident staff; for the employer, failure to withhold can trigger fines from 50% to 3 times the uncollected tax amount and forced collection from corporate bank accounts

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) is compulsorily subject to an independent statutory audit every year regardless of size, revenue, balance-sheet total or headcount; no size-based exemption exists for this entity classification under the PRC Foreign Investment Law, SAMR integrated annual reporting rules, and accounting oversight requirements. For broader PRC domestic companies, an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory if any of the following quantitative or qualitative triggers is met: (i) total assets exceed RMB 20,000,000 (approximately USD 2,760,000); (ii) annual operating turnover exceeds RMB 30,000,000 (approximately USD 4,140,000); (iii) average workforce exceeds 200 employees; (iv) the enterprise is a listed company, financial institution, insurance institution, state-owned enterprise, or is otherwise designated by law as a public-interest entity; (v) the enterprise is subject to a licensed or foreign-investment regulatory regime (including executive-search/headhunting WFOEs), which requires audited financial statements; (vi) the shareholder register, articles of association, lender, investor, or applicable anti-money-laundering obligation requires an audited financial report; (vii) tax authorities select the enterprise for high-risk transfer-pricing audit because related-party revenue or physical transactions exceed the administrative reporting thresholds, requiring contemporaneous documentation of an audited character.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (PRC ASBE/Chinese GAAP), which are substantially converged with IFRS; the WFOE must apply full PRC ASBE for statutory reporting and SAMR/MOFCOM annual filings; tax accounting follows the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law and implementation regulations; the consolidated SME Accounting Standards are available only to qualifying small domestic companies and are not an acceptable framework for a WFOE without regulatory approval.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PRC Foreign Investment Information Reporting system and SAMR integrated annual report, the WFOE must confirm and disclose all current shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, actual controllers, and equity structures in the annual report filed on or before June 30. Any shareholding transfer or change in the ultimate beneficial owner must be registered with SAMR within 30 calendar days of the transaction; for foreign-invested share transfers, the change must also be captured in the next applicable MOFCOM/SAFE foreign-exchange information modification. The company is required to maintain an internal updated shareholder register and beneficial-control record available for SAMR, MOFCOM, SAFE, and tax authorities upon request; there is no standalone government UBO certificate, but privacy/PBOC anti-money-laundering rules require the company to identify beneficial owners during annual KYC reviews and within 5 working days of a competent-law-enforcement request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges/Mortgages (Security Interest and Pledge Register)
Minute Book (Shareholders' Meeting and Board Meeting Minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - USD 3,500 per annum depending on city tier, office-provider arrangement, and whether an independently-certified registered address package must include license-support documentation and inspection coordination for the Human Resources Service License; a full WFOE secretarial agent package typically ranges from USD 1,200 to USD 4,500 per annum.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 12,000 for a single executive-search/headhunting WFOE with low-to-moderate turnover; rising to USD 18,000 - USD 35,000 if a consolidated group audit, transfer-pricing documentation, or MOFCOM/FDI audit special procedure is required.
